- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast marginally, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves in history (e.g., 73+), then corrects — apply downward bias in next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust — apply early correction to avoid prolonged overestimation.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecast values are above 70.5, reduce by 0.5–1.0 unit unless sentiment strongly supports.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag true price by 1–3 days — adjust forecast to align with recent 7–10 day trend, not just 18-day history.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending down, model often undercorrects — add 0.3–0.7 unit upward bias to avoid premature bottoming.
